discovery: Neutron-star mergers as the cosmic site of r-process nucleosynthesis: prediction and theory of kilonovae, confirmed by GW170817

nominees.name: Brian D. Metzger
nominees.affiliation: Columbia University and Flatiron Institute, USA

nominees.name: Daniel Kasen
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

motivation: Where the heaviest elements, from gold to uranium, are made was one of the great open questions of physics for six decades. Lattimer (with Schramm, 1974) first proposed that decompressed neutron-star matter from compact-object mergers forges r-process nuclei. Metzger (2010) showed that radioactive decay of freshly synthesized r-process nuclei powers a distinct optical/infrared transient, the kilonova, and predicted its luminosity and timescale. Kasen (2013) demonstrated that lanthanide opacities make kilonovae red and long-lived, providing the decisive spectral signature. In August 2017 the kilonova accompanying GW170817 matched these predictions, directly witnessing heavy-element production in a merger. Together with the r-process abundance patterns of ancient metal-poor stars and single-event enrichment of ultra-faint dwarf galaxies, this work unites nuclear physics, gravitational-wave astronomy and stellar archaeology into a data-driven account of the origin of the heaviest elements.
